 IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BENGALURU
 DATED THIS THE 19TH DAY OF JANUARY, 2023
 PRESENT
 THE HON'BLE MR JUSTICE ALOK ARADHE
 AND
 THE HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY
 M.F.A. NO.2800/2017 (IDA)
 BETWEEN:

by B A

KUMAR S/O LATE GEORGE P.T.
Location: High

Karnataka R/A UP-STAIRS
 311/55, 6TH CROSS
 VENKATAPURA
 KORAMANGALA
 BANGALORE - 560 034. ...APPELLANT

 (BY SMT. RADHIKA M, ADV.)

 AND:

 SMT. SALAMMA
 W/O P.G. RAJU
 AGED ABOUT 51 YEARS
 R/A GROUND FLOOR
 #311/55, 6TH CORSS
 VENKATAPURA
 KORAMANGALA
 BANGALORE - 506 034. ...RESPONDENT

 (BY SRI THOMAS V PETER, ADV.)

 THIS M.F.A. IS FILED UNDER SECTION 55(1) OF THE DIVORCE
 ACT READ WITH UNDER SECTION 19(1) OF FAMILY COURT ACT
 1984, PRAYING AGAINST THE JUDGEMENT AND DECREE DATED
 22.03.2017 PASSED IN M.C.NO. 2987 OF 2013 ON THE FILE OF THE
 PRINCIPAL JUDGE, FAMILY COURT, BENGALURU, DISMISSING THE
 PETITION FILED UNDER SECTION 10(1)(x) OF THE DIVORCE ACT,
 1869.

 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING THIS DAY,
 VISHWAJITH SHETTY J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




 JUDGMENT

This Miscellaneous First Appeal under Section 19(1) of the

Family Courts Act, 1984 is filed by the appellant-husband

assailing the judgment and decree dated 22.03.2017 passed in

M.C.No.2987/2013 by the Principal Judge, Family Court,

Bangalore dismissing his petition filed under Section 10(x) of

the Divorce Act, 1869 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of

1869') wherein he had sought the relief of dissolution of the

marriage that was solemnized between the parties on

23.10.1989, by a decree of divorce.
2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

3. Brief facts as revealed from the records that may be

relevant for the purpose of disposal of this appeal are, the

marriage of the appellant with the respondent was solemnized

on 23.10.1989 at St. Joseph's Church, Calicut, Kerala in the

presence of their family members. The parties knew each other

even before their marriage and it was a love cum arranged

marriage. The appellant was working at Durgapur, West Bengal

at the time of marriage. Immediately after the marriage, the

couple left to Durgapur and started residing there. The

respondent conceived while she was in Durgapura and when
 -3-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




she was in her fifth month of pregnancy she had returned to

her parent's house. It is the case of the appellant that the

respondent started doubting his fidelity and therefore, she

insisted that he should return to Bengaluru. The appellant

therefore shifted his employment from Durgapur to Bengaluru

and the respondent had joined him at Bengaluru along with

their newly born son. The respondent allegedly started making

reckless allegation against the appellant that he was having an

illicit relationship with the daughter of landlady namely Sheril.

The respondent was also allegedly in the habit of leaving the

house without informing the appellant and the custody of the

minor child was given to maid servant. In the month of

February, 1995 the respondent conceived for the second time

and gave birth to a male child. The appellant out of his

earnings had purchased site at Venkatapura in their joint name

and constructed a house by obtaining a loan and portion of loan

amount was allegedly misused by the respondent and she had

purchased a property in her own name without the knowledge

the appellant. The respondent allegedly behaved in a rude

manner, was in the habit of abusing the appellant and was

making reckless allegations. The appellant resultantly suffered
 -4-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




a heart attack and in spite of the same, the respondent refused

to take care of him and did not bother even to provide him the

basic comfort of life. It is also the case of the appellant that the

respondent allegedly took away the children from him and at

the instance of the respondent on 13.05.2012, the elders son

had assaulted the appellant resulting in fracture of bone on the

nose bridge. Since the relationship between the parties got

strained, they started residing separately and it is under these

circumstances the appellant had filed M.C.No.2987/2013 with a

prayer for dissolution of his marriage on the ground of cruelty.

4. The respondent had appeared in the said

proceedings and filed her detailed statement of objections

denying the allegations made by the appellant. However, she

contended that the appellant had illicit relationship with sheril

who was the daughter of their landlady. She further averred

that the appellant was also having illicit relationship with their

maid Prathibha. She further contended that after coming to

know about this relationship, she had asked the said maid to

leave their house but the appellant had brought her back and

kept her in a paying guest accommodation. She had further

alleged that the appellant was abusing and assaulting her for
 -5-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




silly reason and she also alleged that on one occasion, the

appellant had tried to kill her by using big chopper and on other

occasion, he attacked the elder son with air gun and also tried

to assault him. She further alleged that on 29.01.2013, the

appellant allegedly ransacked her office and in this regard, she

had lodged a complaint against the appellant. The respondent

contended that she is the absolute owner of the entire building

wherein they were residing and the appellant does not have

any right over the same and accordingly, she prayed to dismiss

the petition.

5. To substantiate his case, the appellant had

examined himself as PW1 and got marked 16 documents as

Ex.P1 to Ex.P16. The respondent examined herself as RW.1 but

no documents were marked on her behalf. The Family Court,

thereafter, heard the arguments on both sides and vide the

impugned judgment and decree had dismissed the petition filed

by the appellant under Section 10(x) of the Act of 1869 and

being aggrieved by the same, the appellant is before this Court.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the

Family Court has failed to properly appreciate the oral and

documentary evidence available on record. She submits that
 -6-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




the respondent was in habit of making baseless allegations

against the appellant alleging that he had extra marital

relationship with various ladies. She submits that the appellant

was not respected in his house and the respondent was in a

habit of abusing him in public which resulted in lowering his

image in neighbourhood. She also submits that the respondent

had filed false criminal cases against the appellant and she had

also filed a suit in O.S.No.44/2013 in respect of the property

which belonged to the appellant. She submits that the

appellant was ill-treated by the respondent in his house and as

a result, he suffered health problems and ultimately he also

suffered a heart attack and therefore, he apprehended it was

not safe for him to continue the relationship with the

respondent. In support of her contention, she has relied upon

the judgment of Kerala High Court in the case of Mary Marget

vs. Jos P Thomas - MAT Appeal No.1119/2015 and also on

the judgment of a division bench of this Court in

M.F.A.No.1708/2015 dated 22/06/2022.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent

submits that the appellant has failed to prove the allegation of

cruelty against the respondent and therefore, the Family Court
 -7-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




was justified in dismissing the petition. He submits that mere

wear and tear in the family life cannot be construed as cruelty

for the purpose of granting a decree of divorce. He submits that

the material on record would go to show that the appellant had

treated the respondent with cruelty and not vice-versa. He

submits that the appellant had not taken care of his wife and

children and the respondent was burdened with the educational

expense of the children who are now practicing advocacates.

He also submits that first son is now married. He also submits

that merely for the reason that parties are residing separately

for the last many year, the same cannot be a ground for

granting decree of divorce and accordingly, he prays to dismiss

the appeal.

8. We have carefully considered the arguments

addressed on behalf of the parties and also perused the

material evidence available on record.

9. The appellant had approached the Family Court

seeking the relief of dissolution of marriage by a decree of

divorce on the ground of cruelty. The cruelty for the purpose of

matrimonial offence would be either physical or mental cruelty.

The "Cruelty" in any form imparted by a spouse in a subsisted
 -8-
 MFA No. 2800 of 2017




manner making the life of other party miserable and making it

totally impossible to continue the marital relationship with the

other spouse, would be a good ground for dissolution of the

marriage between the said parties. The appellant herein has

mainly alleged about the mental cruelty inflicted on him by the

respondent by making baseless and false allegation of

unchastity against him. In his pleading he has specifically

stated that the respondent was making false allegation that he

had a illicit relationship with the daughter of landlady, namely

Sheril. The respondent in her statement of objections had not

only reiterated that appellant had a illicit relationship with the

aforesaid Sheril, but he also had extra marital relationship with

their house maid Prathibha.

10. It is trite law that unsubstantiated accusation,

unfounded allegations and character assassination by one

spouse as against the other spouse would amount to mental

cruelty. The Division Bench of Kerala High Court in the case of

 Mary Marget (supra) which arose from a petition filed under

 Section 10 of the Divorce Act alleging cruelty, at paragraph

Nos.10 and 27 has observed as follows:-
MFA No. 2800 of 2017

"10. In matrimonial life, cruelty can be defined in
many ways. It has many perspectives which depend
upon the socio- economic status and circumstances of
parties to the marriage. It varies from person to
person. It also varies with time, place, economic status
and other circumstances. Cruelty can be physical and
mental. Physical cruelty provides more of a direct
evidence, that it can be perceptible when compared to
mental cruelty. Mental cruelty can be drawn from the
facts and circumstances of the case, whereas physical
cruelty can be drawn from the conduct of one spouse
towards other spouse which endangers the other
spouse's physical health. It is true that, mere trivial
irritations, quarrels, normal wear and tear of the married
life which happens in day-to-day life would not be
adequate for grant of divorce on the ground of mental
cruelty. The married life should be reviewed as a whole,
and an few isolated instances over a period fo years will
not amount to cruelty."

"27. This Court, in A:husband vs. B:Wife
(2010) (4) KLT 434) held that the 'nature of cruelty
which would entitle a spouse in matrimony for divorce
must certainly be identical in all religions. Law cannot
recognise different varieties of cruelty as Hindu cruelty,
Muslim cruelty, Christian cruelty or secular cruelty to
justify a decree for divorce. The mere fact that Hindu
Marriage Act and the Special Marriage Act refer to
cruetly without any rider or explanation or the fact that
the Divorce Act and the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage
Act give indication of the nature of matrimonial cruelty
that ought to be established, cannot justify the
conclusion that the nature matrimonial cruelty which
would entitle the spouses for divorce is different under
different personal laws. It would be absolutely safe to
draw inspiration from Art.44 of the Constitution also to
jump to the conclusion that nature of cruelty justifying a
divorce cannot be different under different personal
laws. To our mind, it appears that matrimonial cruelty
must have a uniform definition or conceptualisation to
justify the founding of a decree for divorce. Under 
S.10(1)(x) , the cruelty must be such as to cause
reasonable apprehension in the mind of the petitioner,
spouse that it would be harmful or injurious for the

petitioner to live with the respondent. The expression
 harmful or injurious cannot be limited to physical harm
 or injury. Anything that would hinder the ability of the
 spouse to blossom into his/her fullness and to enjoy life
 in matrimony must be held to fall within the sweep of
 S.10(1)(x) of the Divorce Act. Cruelty which is not
 defined in S.13(1)(1a) of the Hindu Marriage Act and
 S.27(1) of the Special Marriage Act and cruelty which is
 explained in S.2(viii) of the Dissolution of Muslim
 Marriage Act and S.10(1)(x) of the Divorce Act must all
 take inspiration from such understanding of matrimonial
 cruelty. We discard the theory that the concept of
 matrimonial cruelty to entitle a spouse for divorce can
 be dissimilar and different for persons belonging to
 different religious faiths merely because different words
 are used in the relevant personal law statutes'."

11. In the case of VIJAYKUMAR RAMACHANDRA

BHATE V. NEELA VIJAYKUMAR BHATE- (2003) 6 SCC 334,

the Hon'ble Supreme Court at paragraph No.7 has observed as

follows:-

"7. The question that requires to be answered first is as to
 whether the averments, accusations and character
 assassination of the wife by the appellant husband in the
 written statement constitutes mental cruelty for sustaining
 the claim for divorce under Section 13(1) (i-a) of the Act.
 The position of law in this regard has come to be well
 settled and declared that levelling disgusting accusations
 of unchastity and indecent familiarity with a person
 outside wedlock and allegations of extramarital
 relationship is a grave assault on the character, honour,
 reputation, status as well as the health of the wife. Such
 aspersions of perfidiousness attributed to the wife, viewed
 in the context of an educated Indian wife and judged by

Indian conditions and standards would amount to worst
 form of insult and cruelty, sufficient by itself to
 substantiate cruelty in law, warranting the claim of the
 wife being allowed. That such allegations made in the
 written statement or suggested in the course of
 examination and by way of cross-examination satisfy the
 requirement of law has also come to be firmly laid down
 by this Court. On going through the relevant portions of
 such allegations, we find that no exception could be taken
 to the findings recorded by the Family Court as well as the
 High Court. We find that they are of such quality,
 magnitude and consequence as to cause mental pain,
 agony and suffering amounting to the reformulated
 concept of cruelty in matrimonial law causing profound
 and lasting disruption and driving the wife to feel deeply
 hurt and reasonably apprehend that it would be
 dangerous for her to live with a husband who was
 taunting her like that and rendered the maintenance of
 matrimonial home impossible."

12. In the case of NARENDRA V. K.MEENA - (2016)

9 SCC 455 the Hon'ble Supreme Court at paragraph No.16 has

observed as follows:

"16. We have carefully gone through the evidence
 but we could not find any reliable evidence to show that
 the appellant had an extra-marital affair with someone.
 Except for the baseless and reckless allegations, there is
 not even the slightest evidence that would suggest that
 there was something like an affair of the appellant with
 the maid named by the respondent. We consider levelling
 of absolutely false allegations and that too, with regard to

an extra-marital life to be quite serious and that can
 surely be a cause for mental cruelty."

13. The Division Bench of Delhi High Court in the case

of JYOTI YADAV V. NEERAJ YADAV - 2022 SCC ONLINE

DEL 795 at paragraph No.11 has held as follows:-

"11. We consider that...... It has repeatedly been
 held that accusations of unchastity or extra marital
 relationship is a grave assault on character, status,
 reputation as well as health of the spouse against whom
 such allegations were made. It causes mental pain, agony
 suffering and tantamount to cruelty. The allegations of
 extra marital affairs in relationship are serious allegations,
 which have to be made with all seriousness. The tendency
 of making false allegations has to be deprecated by the
 Courts...."

14. The respondent who has made allegation against

the appellant that he was having illicit relationship with various

ladies has failed to prove the same before the Family Court.

Except making such allegations in her pleading and also during

cross-examination of the appellant, she has not attempted to

prove the said allegation made by her against the appellant.

She has not taken steps either to examine the daughter of their

landlady namely Sheril or the housemaid namely Prathibha.

She has also not examined any other independent witness in

respect of the allegation made by her against the appellant that

he had extra marital relationship with other ladies.

15. The material on record would go to show that, in

addition to making this unfounded, baseless allegations of

unchastity and extramarital relationship, the respondent had

also filed various criminal and civil cases against the appellant.

The material on record would also go to show that the parties

were quarrelling with each other and they have no mutual

respect or faith. In addition to the same, the material on record

would also go to show that the parties are residing separately

for the last nearly 10 years.

16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SAMAR

GHOSH V. JAYA GHOSH- (2007) 4 SCC 511 has held as

follows:-

"(XIV) Where there has been a long period of
 continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that the
 matrimonial bond is beyond repair. The marriage
 becomes a fiction though supported by a legal tie. By
 refusing to sever that tie, the law in such cases, does not
 serve the sanctity of marriage; on the contrary, it shows
 scant regard for the feelings and emotions of the parties.
In such like situations, it may lead to mental cruelty."

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of

 K.SRINIVAS RAO V. D.A.DEEPA - AIR 2013 SC 2176 at

paragraph No.16 has held as follows:-

"16. Thus, to the instances illustrative of mental
 cruelty noted in Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh , 2007 (4)
 SCC 511, we could add a few more. Making unfounded
 indecent defamatory allegations against the spouse or his
 or her relatives in the pleadings, filing of complaints or
 issuing notices or news items which may have adverse
 impact on the business prospect or the job of the spouse
 and filing repeated false complaints and cases in the court
 against the spouse would, in the facts of a case, amount
 to causing mental cruelty to the other spouse."
18. In the case of RAVI KUMAR V. JULMIDEVI -

(2010) 4 SCC 476, the Hon'ble Supreme Court at paragraph

No.19 has observed as follows:-

"19. It may be true that there is no definition of
 cruelty under the said Act. Actually such a definition is not
 possible. In matrimonial relationship, cruelty would
 obviously mean absence of mutual respect and
 understanding between the spouses which embitters the
 relationship and often leads to various outbursts of
 behaviour which can be termed as cruelty. Sometime
 cruelty in a matrimonial relationship may take the form of
 violence, sometime it may take a different form. At times,
 it may be just an attitude or an approach. Silence in some
 situations may amount to cruelty."

19. From the aforesaid judgments pronounced by the

Hon'ble Supreme Court it is clear that cruelty in matrimonial

cases could be in different form and it defies definition and

there cannot be any straight jacket formula categorizing the

forms of cruelty. In a given case, whether the husband is cruel

or the wife is cruel has to be ascertained by the Court, based

on the oral and documentary evidence that is placed before it.

It is the duty of the Court to appreciate the evidence placed

before it in the background of settled position of law and

thereafter granted appropriate relief to the parties.

20. In the present case, the material on record would

go to show that the respondent has made baseless and reckless

allegations against the appellant alleging that he had

extramarital relationship with various women and in addition to

the same, she also had indulged in filing multiple criminal

complaints against him and virtually has made his life

miserable. The allegation of cruelty made by the respondent

against the appellant has not been proved by her in the manner

known to law and except her self-serving statement, there is no

other corroborative evidence to believe her version. Under the

circumstances, we are of the considered view that the Family

Court was not justified in dismissing the petition filed by the

appellant under Section 10(x) of the Act, 1869 seeking relief of

dissolution of his marriage that was solemnized on23.10.1989

on the ground of cruelty and therefore, the impugned judgment

and decree passed by the learned Judge of the Family Court

cannot be sustained. Accordingly, the following :-
::ORDER::
Miscellaneous First Appeal is allowed.

The judgment and decree dated

 22.03.2017 passed in M.C.No.2987/2013 by

 the learned Judge of the Family Court,

 Bengaluru is set-aside and consequently, the

 petition filed by the appellant/husband in

 M.C.No.2987/2013 under Section 10(x) of the

 Divorce Act, 1869 is allowed and the marriage

 between the parties that was solemnized on

 23.10.1989 stands dissolved by a decree of

 divorce.
SD/-

JUDGE

 SD/-

JUDGE

NMS

mainly alleged about the mental cruelty inflicted on him by the

respondent by making baseless and false allegation of

unchastity against him. In his pleading he has specifically

stated that the respondent was making false allegation that he

had a illicit relationship with the daughter of landlady, namely

Sheril. The respondent in her statement of objections had not

only reiterated that appellant had a illicit relationship with the

aforesaid Sheril, but he also had extra marital relationship with

their house maid Prathibha.

[p_16] 10. It is trite law that unsubstantiated accusation,

unfounded allegations and character assassination by one

spouse as against the other spouse would amount to mental

cruelty. The Division Bench of Kerala High Court in the case of

 Mary Marget (supra) which arose from a petition filed under

 Section 10 of the Divorce Act alleging cruelty, at paragraph

Nos.10 and 27 has observed as follows:-

[p_17] MFA No. 2800 of 2017

[blockquote_1] "10. In matrimonial life, cruelty can be defined in
many ways. It has many perspectives which depend
upon the socio- economic status and circumstances of
parties to the marriage. It varies from person to
person. It also varies with time, place, economic status
and other circumstances. Cruelty can be physical and
mental. Physical cruelty provides more of a direct
evidence, that it can be perceptible when compared to
mental cruelty. Mental cruelty can be drawn from the
facts and circumstances of the case, whereas physical
cruelty can be drawn from the conduct of one spouse
towards other spouse which endangers the other
spouse's physical health. It is true that, mere trivial
irritations, quarrels, normal wear and tear of the married
life which happens in day-to-day life would not be
adequate for grant of divorce on the ground of mental
cruelty. The married life should be reviewed as a whole,
and an few isolated instances over a period fo years will
not amount to cruelty."

[blockquote_2] "27. This Court, in A:husband vs. B:Wife
(2010) (4) KLT 434) held that the 'nature of cruelty
which would entitle a spouse in matrimony for divorce
must certainly be identical in all religions. Law cannot
recognise different varieties of cruelty as Hindu cruelty,
Muslim cruelty, Christian cruelty or secular cruelty to
justify a decree for divorce. The mere fact that Hindu
Marriage Act and the Special Marriage Act refer to
cruetly without any rider or explanation or the fact that
the Divorce Act and the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage
Act give indication of the nature of matrimonial cruelty
that ought to be established, cannot justify the
conclusion that the nature matrimonial cruelty which
would entitle the spouses for divorce is different under
different personal laws. It would be absolutely safe to
draw inspiration from Art.44 of the Constitution also to
jump to the conclusion that nature of cruelty justifying a
divorce cannot be different under different personal
laws. To our mind, it appears that matrimonial cruelty
must have a uniform definition or conceptualisation to
justify the founding of a decree for divorce. Under 
S.10(1)(x) , the cruelty must be such as to cause
reasonable apprehension in the mind of the petitioner,
spouse that it would be harmful or injurious for the

[blockquote_3] - 10 -

[p_18] petitioner to live with the respondent. The expression
 harmful or injurious cannot be limited to physical harm
 or injury. Anything that would hinder the ability of the
 spouse to blossom into his/her fullness and to enjoy life
 in matrimony must be held to fall within the sweep of
 S.10(1)(x) of the Divorce Act. Cruelty which is not
 defined in S.13(1)(1a) of the Hindu Marriage Act and
 S.27(1) of the Special Marriage Act and cruelty which is
 explained in S.2(viii) of the Dissolution of Muslim
 Marriage Act and S.10(1)(x) of the Divorce Act must all
 take inspiration from such understanding of matrimonial
 cruelty. We discard the theory that the concept of
 matrimonial cruelty to entitle a spouse for divorce can
 be dissimilar and different for persons belonging to
 different religious faiths merely because different words
 are used in the relevant personal law statutes'."

[p_19] 11. In the case of VIJAYKUMAR RAMACHANDRA

BHATE V. NEELA VIJAYKUMAR BHATE- (2003) 6 SCC 334,

the Hon'ble Supreme Court at paragraph No.7 has observed as

follows:-

[blockquote_4] "7. The question that requires to be answered first is as to
 whether the averments, accusations and character
 assassination of the wife by the appellant husband in the
 written statement constitutes mental cruelty for sustaining
 the claim for divorce under Section 13(1) (i-a) of the Act.
 The position of law in this regard has come to be well
 settled and declared that levelling disgusting accusations
 of unchastity and indecent familiarity with a person
 outside wedlock and allegations of extramarital
 relationship is a grave assault on the character, honour,
 reputation, status as well as the health of the wife. Such
 aspersions of perfidiousness attributed to the wife, viewed
 in the context of an educated Indian wife and judged by

[blockquote_5] - 11 -

[blockquote_6] Indian conditions and standards would amount to worst
 form of insult and cruelty, sufficient by itself to
 substantiate cruelty in law, warranting the claim of the
 wife being allowed. That such allegations made in the
 written statement or suggested in the course of
 examination and by way of cross-examination satisfy the
 requirement of law has also come to be firmly laid down
 by this Court. On going through the relevant portions of
 such allegations, we find that no exception could be taken
 to the findings recorded by the Family Court as well as the
 High Court. We find that they are of such quality,
 magnitude and consequence as to cause mental pain,
 agony and suffering amounting to the reformulated
 concept of cruelty in matrimonial law causing profound
 and lasting disruption and driving the wife to feel deeply
 hurt and reasonably apprehend that it would be
 dangerous for her to live with a husband who was
 taunting her like that and rendered the maintenance of
 matrimonial home impossible."

[p_21] 12. In the case of NARENDRA V. K.MEENA - (2016)

9 SCC 455 the Hon'ble Supreme Court at paragraph No.16 has

observed as follows:

[blockquote_7] "16. We have carefully gone through the evidence
 but we could not find any reliable evidence to show that
 the appellant had an extra-marital affair with someone.
 Except for the baseless and reckless allegations, there is
 not even the slightest evidence that would suggest that
 there was something like an affair of the appellant with
 the maid named by the respondent. We consider levelling
 of absolutely false allegations and that too, with regard to

[blockquote_8] - 12 -

[blockquote_9] an extra-marital life to be quite serious and that can
 surely be a cause for mental cruelty."

[p_23] 13. The Division Bench of Delhi High Court in the case

of JYOTI YADAV V. NEERAJ YADAV - 2022 SCC ONLINE

DEL 795 at paragraph No.11 has held as follows:-

[blockquote_10] "11. We consider that...... It has repeatedly been
 held that accusations of unchastity or extra marital
 relationship is a grave assault on character, status,
 reputation as well as health of the spouse against whom
 such allegations were made. It causes mental pain, agony
 suffering and tantamount to cruelty. The allegations of
 extra marital affairs in relationship are serious allegations,
 which have to be made with all seriousness. The tendency
 of making false allegations has to be deprecated by the
 Courts...."

[p_24] 14. The respondent who has made allegation against

the appellant that he was having illicit relationship with various

ladies has failed to prove the same before the Family Court.

Except making such allegations in her pleading and also during

cross-examination of the appellant, she has not attempted to

prove the said allegation made by her against the appellant.

She has not taken steps either to examine the daughter of their

landlady namely Sheril or the housemaid namely Prathibha.

She has also not examined any other independent witness in

respect of the allegation made by her against the appellant that

he had extra marital relationship with other ladies.

[p_25] - 13 -

[p_27] 15. The material on record would go to show that, in

addition to making this unfounded, baseless allegations of

unchastity and extramarital relationship, the respondent had

also filed various criminal and civil cases against the appellant.

The material on record would also go to show that the parties

were quarrelling with each other and they have no mutual

respect or faith. In addition to the same, the material on record

would also go to show that the parties are residing separately

for the last nearly 10 years.

[p_29] 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SAMAR

GHOSH V. JAYA GHOSH- (2007) 4 SCC 511 has held as

follows:-

[blockquote_11] "(XIV) Where there has been a long period of
 continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that the
 matrimonial bond is beyond repair. The marriage
 becomes a fiction though supported by a legal tie. By
 refusing to sever that tie, the law in such cases, does not
 serve the sanctity of marriage; on the contrary, it shows
 scant regard for the feelings and emotions of the parties.

[p_31] In such like situations, it may lead to mental cruelty."

[p_32] 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of

 K.SRINIVAS RAO V. D.A.DEEPA - AIR 2013 SC 2176 at

paragraph No.16 has held as follows:-

[blockquote_12] - 14 -

[blockquote_13] "16. Thus, to the instances illustrative of mental
 cruelty noted in Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh , 2007 (4)
 SCC 511, we could add a few more. Making unfounded
 indecent defamatory allegations against the spouse or his
 or her relatives in the pleadings, filing of complaints or
 issuing notices or news items which may have adverse
 impact on the business prospect or the job of the spouse
 and filing repeated false complaints and cases in the court
 against the spouse would, in the facts of a case, amount
 to causing mental cruelty to the other spouse."

[p_33] 18. In the case of RAVI KUMAR V. JULMIDEVI -

[p_34] (2010) 4 SCC 476, the Hon'ble Supreme Court at paragraph

No.19 has observed as follows:-

[p_36] "19. It may be true that there is no definition of
 cruelty under the said Act. Actually such a definition is not
 possible. In matrimonial relationship, cruelty would
 obviously mean absence of mutual respect and
 understanding between the spouses which embitters the
 relationship and often leads to various outbursts of
 behaviour which can be termed as cruelty. Sometime
 cruelty in a matrimonial relationship may take the form of
 violence, sometime it may take a different form. At times,
 it may be just an attitude or an approach. Silence in some
 situations may amount to cruelty."

[p_38] 19. From the aforesaid judgments pronounced by the

Hon'ble Supreme Court it is clear that cruelty in matrimonial

cases could be in different form and it defies definition and

there cannot be any straight jacket formula categorizing the

forms of cruelty. In a given case, whether the husband is cruel

or the wife is cruel has to be ascertained by the Court, based

[p_39] - 15 -

[p_40] on the oral and documentary evidence that is placed before it.

It is the duty of the Court to appreciate the evidence placed

before it in the background of settled position of law and

thereafter granted appropriate relief to the parties.

[p_41] 20. In the present case, the material on record would

go to show that the respondent has made baseless and reckless

allegations against the appellant alleging that he had

extramarital relationship with various women and in addition to

the same, she also had indulged in filing multiple criminal

complaints against him and virtually has made his life

miserable. The allegation of cruelty made by the respondent

against the appellant has not been proved by her in the manner

known to law and except her self-serving statement, there is no

other corroborative evidence to believe her version. Under the

circumstances, we are of the considered view that the Family

Court was not justified in dismissing the petition filed by the

appellant under Section 10(x) of the Act, 1869 seeking relief of

dissolution of his marriage that was solemnized on23.10.1989

on the ground of cruelty and therefore, the impugned judgment

and decree passed by the learned Judge of the Family Court

cannot be sustained. Accordingly, the following :-

[blockquote_14] - 16 -

[blockquote_15] ::ORDER::

[blockquote_16] Miscellaneous First Appeal is allowed.

[blockquote_17] The judgment and decree dated

 22.03.2017 passed in M.C.No.2987/2013 by

 the learned Judge of the Family Court,

 Bengaluru is set-aside and consequently, the

 petition filed by the appellant/husband in

 M.C.No.2987/2013 under Section 10(x) of the

 Divorce Act, 1869 is allowed and the marriage

 between the parties that was solemnized on

 23.10.1989 stands dissolved by a decree of

 divorce.
